scope: 36 ordered sampled PNGs for coast and fleet in phone and fallback tiers.
verdict: Positive against the prior ring-marked and heavier tree-shadow samples. Open brackets preserve player tracking, label clearance holds at both edge cases, and trees are more grounded without a new visual distraction.
remaining: The runway still shows a separate faint circle during the return sequence.
The white hit silhouette still wipes airframe detail at 006 and 012.
The gray-blue plane still competes with the carrier deck and dark or blue offset shapes over water remain ambiguous.

coast-fallback-000.png.evidence: Tree bases read more distinctly along the approach and access road. The open brackets locate the player over the tarmac.

coast-fallback-006.png.evidence: The solid-white hit feedback still erases airframe detail briefly, while the separate faint runway circle is visible below.

coast-fallback-012.png.evidence: Bright hit silhouette stays separate from the Hawk label and orange sparks. Foliage has more compact shadow footprints.

coast-fallback-024.png.evidence: Normal aircraft colors return. Brackets avoid occluding the runway threshold and trees retain compact shadows.

coast-fallback-036.png.evidence: Thin player profile is easier to track with brackets as it passes the runway end. Foliage contact still reads.

coast-fallback-060.png.evidence: Compact foliage shadows and layered shoreline stay readable behind the fireball. Brackets keep player ownership clear.

coast-fallback-090.png.evidence: Blast fades to specks and the bracketed player tracks over water. The tree near Hawk stays visually grounded.

coast-fallback-120.png.evidence: Paired tracers remain clear against dark water and the separate runway circle is still visible.

coast-fallback-180.png.evidence: Hawk label clears the Return to Base banner in both tiers. Smaller shadows reduce the pooled darkness below trees.
